gloss.lead: Here is every word from the lessons, each tagged with the unit it came from and paired with a short example that uses only words you have already met. Tap a word or a card to hear it. “Answers: hidden” at the top right covers the meanings so you can use these as flashcards. Below you can search or filter by unit.
gloss.empty: No matching word — try a different search.

review.setup_sub: Questions generated · tap to answer · missed words come back
review.lead: The questions follow three ordinary principles: recalling rather than re-reading, mixing units together instead of drilling them in blocks, and showing the answer at once so the word can come round again. A wrong answer costs nothing — you just see the word once more.
review.need_more: Pick a scope first (at least 4 words)
review.note_body: What you learned most recently fades fastest, which is why the last two units are selected by default. After a few days, switch the scope to “All” for a random check. Mixed mode warms up with easy meaning questions before adding listening and recall.
review.fnote: Gapapa — no harm done. This word will come round again shortly.
review.praise_mid: Bagus! Most of it has stuck — clear up the few you missed.
review.praise_lo: Gapapa — run “missed words only” once more; each pass helps.
review.wrong_title: Worth another look (tap a card to hear it)

drill.setup_sub: Practise saying it, not just recognising it
drill.lead: Review mode checks that you know what a word means. This one trains answering on the spot — so that when someone asks where you are from, where you live, or what your name is, the answer is already there. Questions are drawn at random, so you practise applying the pattern rather than memorising one answer.
drill.need_type: Choose at least one question type
drill.note_body: Fifteen questions as a warm-up before the vocabulary review makes an easy sequence. Wrong answers cost nothing; anything you miss comes back once at the end of the round.
drill.cue_jam: How do you say this time?
drill.cue_angka: How do you read this number?
drill.why_jam: Remember: half past is “half of the next hour”. 1:30 is setengah dua, not setengah satu.
drill.why_angka: Read it place by place: thousands, then hundreds, then tens — the same order as in English.
drill.why_other: Gapapa — this one comes back at the end of the round.
drill.praise_mid: Bagus! You've got the idea — tidy up the ones you missed.
drill.praise_lo: Gapapa — run “missed questions only” once more; it gets easier each pass.
